incident-bot: [ALERT] Rapid increase in TLS handshake failures (ssl.alert) and 502/504s observed for api.redwood.example.com. Error rate jumped to ~25% starting 2026-05-10T17:04Z. Paging on-call: @Lena G. :rotating_light:

Lena G: I'm oncall. Seeing support surge. What changed in last hour?

deploy-bot: Recent events: 2026-05-10T16:45Z cert-manager rotated certs for api.redwood.example.com; 2026-05-10T16:50Z edge-proxy:v3.18.0 rolled to 30% canary; 2026-05-10T16:55Z peering config pushed to transit provider (adjusted MTU and BGP communities).

Jamie C: support sample: customers report immediate "handshake failure" then 504 on retries. Corporate proxies and a subset of ISPs most affected. Mobile networks less impacted.

Lena G: pulling ELB/ALB logs and edge proxy logs now. Anyone see cert errors?

Priya S: ALB ack: some edge IPs presenting the new cert chain; others return only the leaf cert. Here's a curl run against two ALB IPs we resolved:
```
$ curl -sI --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:198.51.100.10 https://api.redwood.example.com/health | grep -i "certificate"
* SSL certificate verify ok.
$ curl -sI --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:198.51.100.22 https://api.redwood.example.com/health
* SSL: no peer certificate
```

Omar K: grabbing tcpdump on peering interface and checking for ICMP frag-needed. Early snippet: 
```
17:04:10.011223 IP 203.0.113.99.52344 > 10.70.12.34.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:1540, length 1539
17:04:10.011224 IP 203.0.113.99 > 10.70.12.34: ICMP 3/4 Frag needed and DF set, mtu 1400
17:04:10.011233 IP 10.70.12.34.443 > 203.0.113.99.52344: Flags [R.], seq 1, ack 1540, length 0
```

Omar K: PMTU blackhole detected on transit hop advertising 1400. Our hosts default to 1500; some clients send MSS 1460 and produce fragmented ClientHellos. A number of middleboxes drop fragments, leading to incomplete TLS handshakes and upstream closes.

Jamie C: openssl from an affected corporate proxy VM shows: 
```
$ openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example.com:443 -servername api.redwood.example.com
CONNECTED(00000003)
140360...:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert certificate unknown:../ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1524:SSL alert number 46
no peer certificate available
```

Priya S: cert-manager logs show a transient API error when attaching the intermediate bundle to the ALB at 16:45:13Z; most nodes succeeded on retry but a few returned 500 then later succeeded. Snippet:
```
2026-05-10T16:45:12Z cert-manager: uploadCert -> 200
2026-05-10T16:45:13Z cert-manager: attachBundle target=198.51.100.22 -> 500 transient
2026-05-10T16:45:14Z cert-manager: attachBundle target=198.51.100.22 -> 200
```

Lena G: hypothesis table in-thread:
- H1: partial cert chain on subset of ALB nodes (evidence: curl showing no peer certificate on some IPs; cert-manager 500s).
- H2: PMTU/MTU mismatch on transit causing fragmented ClientHello and dropped fragments -> handshake failures (evidence: ICMP frag-needed and RSTs in tcpdump).
- H3: interplay between canary edge-proxy rollout and cert propagation causing uneven client behavior.

Omar K: immediate mitigations proposed: (a) re-run forced cert attach across all ALB nodes to ensure full chain; (b) apply MSS clamp on peering gateways to 1360 to avoid fragmentation; (c) hold canary and shift traffic away from nodes with missing chain. Which to prioritize?

Priya S: cert attach is low-risk and quick. I'll force-attach and then verify across all edge IPs. Lena, can you coordinate traffic hold if needed?

Lena G: doing cert attach first. Priya, drop commands/logs here.

Priya S: forcing attach now. Command: `aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn ... --certificates CertificateArn=...,CertificateChain=/fullchain.pem` (run via orchestration).

deploy-bot: cert attach job started by Priya S at 2026-05-10T17:12Z.

Omar K: while that's running, I'm applying MSS clamp on peering routers (example):
```
# VyOS example
set firewall name MSS-CLAMP rule 10 action modify
set firewall name MSS-CLAMP rule 10 tcp-mss 1360
commit
```

Omar K: MSS clamp applied at 17:14Z. Monitoring tcpdump: fragmentation count falls sharply.

Priya S: cert attach finished 17:15Z. Re-checking ALB IPs via curl: all probed IPs now present full chain.

Jamie C: support update: customer reports decreasing. Some proxy-heavy customers saw immediate improvement after the network change + cert fix.

Lena G: validation: synthetic checks from EU/ASIA show TLS handshake error rate down to 0.7% after mitigations. Rolling hold on edge-proxy canary and continuing monitoring.

Omar K: long-term actions we should track: 1) negotiate MTU alignment with transit provider or ensure PMTU works (they appear to be dropping ICMP for DF); 2) add MSS clamp as part of peering baseline or auto-apply when path MTU changes; 3) add monitoring for ICMP frag-needed trends and per-path MSS mismatches.

Priya S: infra follow-ups: 1) make cert-manager attachment idempotent and add end-to-end verification that every ALB node has full chain before finishing rotation; 2) add a preflight check to the cert rotation job that queries multiple edge IPs (including behind proxies) for full chain; 3) add automation to detect and retry transient attachBundle failures and flag manual review if >2 retries.

Lena G: timeline in-thread (concise):
- 16:45 cert-manager rotate started
- 16:50 edge-proxy:v3.18.0 canary roll began
- 16:55 peering MTU change pushed to transit provider
- 17:04 monitoring spike TLS handshake failures/502s
- 17:07 tcpdump shows frag-needed + RSTs; curl shows partial chains on some ALB IPs
- 17:12 forced cert attach initiated
- 17:14 MSS clamp applied to peering
- 17:15 cert attach completed; synthetic checks resumed and improving

Jamie C: impact summary: ~70 customers intermittently affected (corporate proxies and some ISPs). Short-duration outages for some clients, overall incident window ~30-45 minutes. We're sending customer follow-ups with mitigation steps.

ops-bot: Artifacts saved to s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/1911111111/{alb-logs,tcpdumps,cert-manager-logs}.zip and Confluence doc https://confluence.internal/redwood/incidents/1911111111

Lena G: assigning postmortem owner: Priya S will lead RCA. Priya, please collect all artifacts and include tests added / deployment pipeline changes.

Priya S: acknowledged. I'll own the RCA and set postmortem due in 48h. Will include root cause evidence (tcpdumps showing frag-needed), cert-manager attach logs, ALB cert state snapshots, and remediation timeline.

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated, assigned -> Priya S for postmortem. Next incident update in 2 hours. :white_check_mark:
